source.citation: Case AL & Barrett SCH (2004). Floral biology of gender monomorphism and dimorphism in Wurmbea dioica (Colchicaceae) in Western Australia. International Journal of Plant Sciences 165(2):289–301.
source.study_site: Sympatric monomorphic and dimorphic populations near Perth, Western Australia; W. dioica ssp. alba
source.data_level: Original article's published rounded group means, reported ranges, and qualitative inferential statements; no raw plant/flower-level observations
source.audit_method: Author PDF full-text extracted by public search and cross-checked against article abstract and Methods; screenshot endpoint returned 404, so visual original-table verification incomplete

observation_design.visit_measure: Fly visit rate per flower during 15-min observation periods

female_seed_to_ovule_reported_ranges.note: Text ranges span reported pollination conditions and are not 95% confidence intervals; do not assign endpoints to specific treatments

limits: The fly visit observations were taken in nonoverlapping dates with different morph-specific floral phenologies; the taxon contrast is not an equal-season intervention
A common sympatric location does not make floral morphs matched treatments, and the two sexual systems constitute different populations
Not the same individuals or flowers observed along the full visit-to-seed pathway; no plant-level covariance or causal mediation is estimable
Mean visit rate excludes honeybee visits; honeybees visited only cosexuals
Seed-to-ovule intervals are ranges reported across pollination regimes and not sampling confidence intervals
Non-significant differences in pollen receipt or pollen-supplementation effect do not establish equivalence or the absence of a small limitation
The cause of low seed fertility (inbreeding, pollen quality, resource availability, predation) was not experimentally resolved by this comparison
No male paternity, outcrossing paternity, genotype-dependent lifetime fitness or directional selection estimates
Cannot infer historical origin, genetic constraint, or SLK Phi/g0/Delta_R from these descriptive source values
Cannot mix western subspecies alba and eastern dioica source estimates as a within-population mechanism or meta-analytic effect
Anther onset, dehiscence duration and first-day pollen removal are separate published metrics; no reconstructed daily pollen time series, paternity success or causal floral-architecture effect

days_from_anthesis_until_first_pollen_pr.note: Males start releasing pollen earlier than cosexuals; source p.293, original means SE

days_to_dehisce_all_six_anthers.note: Source p.293; male dehiscence is more prolonged

first_day_percent_of_total_pollen_remove.note: Source pp.294–297; first pollen-presentation day, not overall nine-day pollen removal

anther_reclosure_after_wet_or_windy_weat.note: Qualitative source observation, not quantified probability or inherited evolutionary innovation
